problem: Which of the following parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ generate a circle of radius $3$ centered at the point $(5,-3)?$

feedback.problem: Which of the following parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ generate a circle of radius $1$ centered at the point $(4,-6)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +a,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +b,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, we have a circle of radius $1$ centered at the point $(4,-6).$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the circle are

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -6,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
